description: Single-panel scatter plot of tensile strength versus elongation to fracture, summarizing selected RAP mechanical-testing results. The x-axis is "elongation to fracture [%]" (0-80); the y-axis is "tensile strength [MPa]" (ticks 500-1000). A boxed header lists the five alloys studied: Fe-30Mn-1.2C; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al. A colour key assigns 0Al = open gray circle, 2Al = pale cyan, 4Al = blue, 6Al = dark navy, 8Al = purple. Annotation text reads "Tempering 450, 500, 550, 600 °C" and "T: 1h  T+t: 24h". The Al-free 0Al series follows a broad dark dashed trend labelled "T + t", rising from about 490 MPa at ~8% elongation to about 800 MPa at ~70% elongation. The 2Al (pale cyan) and 4Al (blue) points form the lowest-strength clusters at roughly 460-600 MPa with elongation spanning ~8% to ~55%. The 6Al (dark navy) points lie between at ~670-770 MPa and ~30-55% elongation. The 8Al (purple) series reaches the highest strength (~800-950 MPa) and is joined by a separate purple dashed "T + t" curve. The figure demonstrates that higher Al content — especially 8 wt.% — and aging shift the alloy toward higher tensile strength at reduced elongation.

observations.observation: The plot axes are 'elongation to fracture [%]' (x, 0-80) and 'tensile strength [MPa]' (y, grid ticks 500-1000).
A boxed header lists the five alloys covered: Fe-30Mn-1.2C; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-2Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-4Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-6Al; Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al.
The colour key maps 0Al to an open/gray circle, 2Al to pale cyan, 4Al to blue, 6Al to dark navy and 8Al to purple filled circles.
Annotation text on the plot reads 'Tempering 450, 500, 550, 600 °C' and 'T: 1h  T+t: 24h'.
The 8Al (purple) points occupy the highest tensile-strength region of the plot, between roughly the 800 and 950 MPa levels.
The 0Al (open gray) points follow a dark dashed curve labelled 'T + t', rising from about 490 MPa near 8% elongation to about 800 MPa near 70% elongation.
The 2Al (pale cyan) and 4Al (blue) points form the lowest-strength clusters, spanning roughly 460-600 MPa.
The 6Al (dark navy) points fall between the extremes, roughly 670-770 MPa at about 30-55% elongation.
A separate purple dashed curve labelled 'T + t' connects the aged 8Al points, which shift toward higher strength at lower elongation.
The caption states the figure reports tensile strength and total elongation for alloys Fe-30Mn-1.2C through Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al, with some data taken from Ref. 49.
The citing text states that 24 h aging of Fe-30Mn-1.2C-8Al raises YS, UTS and hardness to about twice the as-homogenized levels while drastically reducing ductility.
The citing text states that alloys with 2-6 wt.% Al show properties between the Al-free and 8 wt.% Al alloys, with the 4 wt.% and 6 wt.% variants only weakly affected by aging.

subfigures.description: Scatter/trend plot of tensile strength (MPa, y) vs. elongation to fracture (%, x) for five Fe-30Mn-1.2C-based alloys (0/2/4/6/8 Al), colour-coded, with two dashed 'T + t' trend curves and an aging/tempering condition annotation.
